access-to-proof.name: Control of evidence
access-to-proof.plain: The records needed to show a violation are held by the party being regulated, so without disclosure, subpoena or preservation powers, enforcers and injured people may be unable to prove a case.
access-to-proof.check: Find who holds the evidence needed to prove a violation. Ask whether the text gives enforcers and private parties access, subpoena power and a duty to preserve records, or leaves proof to the regulated party.
access-to-proof.fix: Add disclosure, subpoena and record preservation powers for enforcers and claimants.
access-to-proof.ex_ai: Companies hold the data needed to prove harm, and without disclosure powers, subpoena authority or preservation duties, regulators and plaintiffs cannot get it.
access-to-proof.ex_other: For illustration: A workplace safety law might rely on employer inspection logs while giving inspectors no power to compel them.

acquisition-thresholds.name: Review triggers that miss most deals
acquisition-thresholds.plain: Review triggers based on price or size can let most transactions pass unexamined, especially where the thing acquired has little or no sale price but large strategic value.
acquisition-thresholds.check: Find the trigger for review of a transaction or entry. Ask what it is measured in, whether low priced or free items can fall below it, and whether data, users or capability could be counted instead.
acquisition-thresholds.fix: Add review triggers based on factors such as users, data or capability, not price alone.
acquisition-thresholds.ex_ai: High thresholds or price-based tests, often zero for free AI products, exempt most acquisitions.
acquisition-thresholds.ex_other: For illustration: A hospital merger review law might trigger only above a dollar value, so purchases of small clinics with large local market share fall outside it.

addictive-design-definition.name: Definition tied to a clinical test
addictive-design-definition.plain: Defining a harmful feature by a clinical or diagnostic standard can leave out features that foster compulsive use but do not meet that standard, so the covered category ends up narrow.
addictive-design-definition.check: Find definitions of harm that depend on a diagnosis, a professional standard or a medical criterion. Ask whether features that cause the same behavior without meeting that test would fall outside the rule.
addictive-design-definition.fix: Define the covered practice by observable design features, with no clinical test.
addictive-design-definition.ex_ai: Tying addictive design to clinical criteria leaves out compulsive-use features, so engaging designs remain allowed while addictive ones are banned.
addictive-design-definition.ex_other: For illustration: A gambling rule might cover only products that cause a diagnosed disorder, leaving similar games without that proof outside it.

adversary-argument.name: Rival framing of restraint
adversary-argument.plain: Presenting each protective rule as helping a competitor or rival can make restraint look like a loss and can crowd out safeguards, even where the claim is untested.
adversary-argument.check: Find statements that tie a safeguard to advantage for a rival nation, firm or sector. Ask what evidence supports the claim and whether the safeguard still operates independently of it.
adversary-argument.fix: Require stated evidence for competitive claims and keep protective duties independent of them.
adversary-argument.ex_ai: Framing every safety rule as helping a rival nation presents restraint as surrender and can crowd out safety measures.
adversary-argument.ex_other: For illustration: A food import safety bill might be argued down on the ground that stricter inspection would hand business to foreign suppliers.

age-verification-poison-pill.name: Burdensome step that invites opposition
age-verification-poison-pill.plain: A required step that is costly, intrusive or hard to carry out can draw broad opposition and stall an otherwise supported bill, or be hard to comply with in practice.
age-verification-poison-pill.check: Find any required verification, registration or documentation step. Ask whether it is feasible, what it costs users and regulated parties, and whether its burden could draw opposition that endangers the whole law.
age-verification-poison-pill.fix: Use a feasible, privacy protective version of the step and keep it severable from the core duties.
age-verification-poison-pill.ex_ai: Requiring age verification that is infeasible or invasive can generate opposition that sinks the whole bill.
age-verification-poison-pill.ex_other: For illustration: A tenant protection bill might require landlords to collect proof of income from every applicant, drawing objections that overshadow its main protections.

aggregation-proof-reporting.name: Reports that cannot be compared
aggregation-proof-reporting.plain: When each regulated party chooses its own reporting format or method, the resulting data cannot be compared, so patterns across the field stay hidden.
aggregation-proof-reporting.check: Find reporting duties. Ask whether the text fixes a common template, metrics and method, or lets each reporter choose, and whether results could be compared across parties and years.
aggregation-proof-reporting.fix: Require a standard template, defined metrics and a common method for all reporters.
aggregation-proof-reporting.ex_ai: Reporting formats that differ between companies produce data that cannot be meaningfully compared.
aggregation-proof-reporting.ex_other: For illustration: A school discipline reporting law might let each district define its own categories, so statewide totals cannot be compared.

ai-dependent-workers.ex_ai: Workers managed by algorithms may not be legally recognized as employees, leaving employment protections outside reach.

ai-system-definition.name: Core definition narrows coverage
ai-system-definition.plain: The definition of the thing regulated sets the law's reach, and one that is too narrow, too technical or tied to a particular design can leave out products people rely on.
ai-system-definition.check: Find the definition that fixes what the law covers. Ask what ordinary products or uses it leaves out, whether it depends on a design feature, and whether a close variant would escape it.
ai-system-definition.fix: Define coverage by function and effect, with clear examples and an update mechanism.
ai-system-definition.ex_ai: A definition limited to large or fully autonomous models leaves out recommendation tools, fine-tuned models and decision support that people rely on.
ai-system-definition.ex_other: For illustration: A drinking water law might define a covered system by pipe diameter, leaving smaller systems that serve many households outside it.

algorithmic-vs-ai-label.name: Label choice sets scope
algorithmic-vs-ai-label.plain: The term chosen to name the regulated thing can make a law look broad while its definition reaches little, or the reverse, depending on what the label is taken to include.
algorithmic-vs-ai-label.check: Find the main label used for the covered subject. Ask what the definition actually includes, whether other terms for similar things are used elsewhere, and whether the label matches the coverage.
algorithmic-vs-ai-label.fix: Use one defined term and test it against the full range of products and practices intended to be covered.
algorithmic-vs-ai-label.ex_ai: Choosing the term algorithmic or AI changes how broad a law appears, and the label can narrow or widen what is covered.
algorithmic-vs-ai-label.ex_other: For illustration: A chemical safety bill might regulate hazardous substances while its definition includes only listed compounds, so a broad title overstates its reach.

api-chokepoint.name: Rules attached to one access point
api-chokepoint.plain: Placing duties on whoever controls a single access point can make that party a gatekeeper and can shape or end other ways the product is distributed.
api-chokepoint.check: Find the point in the supply or access chain where duties attach. Ask who controls it, what the duty gives them power to refuse, and what other distribution routes the rule affects.
api-chokepoint.fix: State what the access point holder must and need not do, and protect lawful alternative routes.
api-chokepoint.ex_ai: Rules at the API level make API controllers gatekeepers and can end open source distribution.
api-chokepoint.ex_other: For illustration: A pharmacy law might place all dispensing duties on wholesalers, making them gatekeepers over which small pharmacies can stock a drug.

arbitration-class-waivers.name: Arbitration and class waivers
arbitration-class-waivers.plain: Mandatory arbitration, class waivers and individual proof requirements stop claims from being joined, which can leave widely shared small harms without any practical remedy.
arbitration-class-waivers.check: Find any limits on how claims are brought. Ask whether pre-dispute arbitration or class waivers can displace the law's remedies, and whether small harms across many people can be pursued together.
arbitration-class-waivers.fix: Bar pre-dispute waivers of the law's remedies and preserve collective actions.
arbitration-class-waivers.ex_ai: Mandatory arbitration, class action waivers and individualized proof requirements prevent claims from being combined, leaving little remedy for widely shared harms.
arbitration-class-waivers.ex_other: For illustration: A consumer lending bill might allow lenders to require individual arbitration, so a small fee charged to thousands is never challenged.

assistance-without-assistance.name: Assistance that does not assist
assistance-without-assistance.plain: Support programs that are underfunded, mismatched to need or hard to qualify for can look like a response to harm while reaching few of the people affected.
assistance-without-assistance.check: Find support or transition programs. Ask what funding, eligibility rules and application steps apply, how many people could realistically qualify, and whether the support matches the loss.
assistance-without-assistance.fix: Fund assistance to match expected need and set simple eligibility and outcome reporting.
assistance-without-assistance.ex_ai: Retraining or support programs that are underfunded, mismatched or hard to qualify for give the appearance of addressing displacement.
assistance-without-assistance.ex_other: For illustration: A plant closure law might offer retraining for jobs that do not exist locally, with enrollment limited to a small number of workers.

audit-scope.name: Audit frequency and scope
audit-scope.plain: Audits that are infrequent or narrow in scope can miss problems that develop between reviews or fall outside the items examined.
audit-scope.check: Find audit or inspection duties. Ask how often they occur, what they cover, who performs them, and whether a fast changing product or practice could pass between audits.
audit-scope.fix: Set review frequency by risk, include change triggered reviews and define full scope and auditor independence.
audit-scope.ex_ai: Annual or narrowly scoped audits miss fast-changing systems and misuse.
audit-scope.ex_other: For illustration: A building safety law might require one inspection every five years of listed items only, missing later repairs and unlisted hazards.

baseline-choice.name: Baseline selection
baseline-choice.plain: Measuring change from a chosen starting point can make a new harm look like a continuation of an existing trend, or hide how much has changed.
baseline-choice.check: Find comparisons to a prior year, level or condition. Ask who picked the baseline, why that point, and how the result would differ if an earlier or later baseline were used.
baseline-choice.fix: State the baseline and the reason for it, and require results against more than one reference point.
baseline-choice.ex_ai: Comparing present conditions to a chosen starting year can make a new harm look like a continuation of existing trends.
baseline-choice.ex_other: For illustration: An emissions bill might measure cuts from a year with unusually high output, so ordinary levels count as progress.

benchmark-gaming.name: Fixed test based compliance
benchmark-gaming.plain: When compliance is shown by passing a fixed test, a party can tune to the test while real world performance stays different.
benchmark-gaming.check: Find tests, scores or standard procedures that count as compliance. Ask whether they are public and fixed, whether performance can be tuned to them, and whether real world results are also checked.
benchmark-gaming.fix: Pair fixed tests with unannounced and real world checks and refresh tests regularly.
benchmark-gaming.ex_ai: Compliance measured by fixed benchmarks can be met by tuning to the test while real-world performance differs.
benchmark-gaming.ex_other: For illustration: A vehicle emissions rule might rely on one laboratory cycle, so engines can be tuned to pass it while road emissions are higher.

bias-is-a-bug.name: Harm treated as a fixable defect
bias-is-a-bug.plain: Describing a harm as a technical defect to be improved can make the remedy a fix by the operator, rather than a limit on where or whether the product is used.
bias-is-a-bug.check: Find language that treats a harm as an error rate or defect. Ask whether the only remedy is improvement, and whether use can be limited, paused or prohibited if the defect persists.
bias-is-a-bug.fix: Provide limits on use and remedies independent of whether the operator claims to have improved the product.
bias-is-a-bug.ex_ai: Framing bias as a technical defect makes the remedy to improve the system and not to limit its use.
bias-is-a-bug.ex_other: For illustration: A lending bill might require lenders to refine scoring methods after disparities appear, with no ability to restrict the method itself.

board-liability.name: No leadership level duties
board-liability.plain: If duties fall only on the organization, no named senior person is answerable, which can change behavior less than personal accountability would.
board-liability.check: Find who must comply and who answers if they do not. Ask whether directors or senior officers have any duty, certification or personal exposure, or only the entity.
board-liability.fix: Add duties, certification or accountability for named senior officers or directors.
board-liability.ex_ai: Without duties at board level, responsibility rests with the company, which changes behavior less than personal accountability.
board-liability.ex_other: For illustration: A financial reporting law might impose penalties on the firm only, with no certification by its chief executive.

challenge-notification.name: No notice of a covered decision
challenge-notification.plain: People who are not told that a covered process shaped a decision about them cannot know they have something to challenge.
challenge-notification.check: Find decisions that affect individuals. Ask whether the person must be told of the decision, the factors used and how to contest it, and when and in what form.
challenge-notification.fix: Require timely plain language notice of the decision, its basis and the route to challenge it.
challenge-notification.ex_ai: Without notice that AI shaped a decision, affected people cannot know they have something to challenge.
challenge-notification.ex_other: For illustration: A benefits eligibility law might let an agency deny claims using an internal screening score without telling applicants it was used.

choosing-regulator.name: Choice of regulator
choosing-regulator.plain: Which agency oversees a subject shapes its priorities and culture, and some choices produce weaker, conflicted or fragmented oversight.
choosing-regulator.check: Find the agency given authority. Ask whether its mission, expertise, funding and past practice fit the subject, and whether authority is divided or placed with a body that favors the regulated sector.
choosing-regulator.fix: Assign authority to a body whose mission fits, with adequate resources and a clear lead.
choosing-regulator.ex_ai: Which agency oversees a subject shapes its culture and priorities, and some choices produce weaker or fragmented oversight.
choosing-regulator.ex_other: For illustration: A pipeline safety bill might place oversight with an agency whose main mission is promoting energy development.

classified-escape.name: Designation that removes public review
classified-escape.plain: A status such as classified or exempt from disclosure can place records outside public review, making records requests and challenges hard or impossible.
classified-escape.check: Find any power to designate material or programs as classified, confidential or exempt from disclosure. Ask who decides, on what standard, and whether any independent review or summary remains.
classified-escape.fix: Require a stated standard, independent review and public summaries for exempt designations.
classified-escape.ex_ai: Systems designated classified fall outside public review, and records requests and challenges become effectively impossible.
classified-escape.ex_other: For illustration: A policing technology bill might exempt any program an official marks sensitive, so its use cannot be requested or reviewed.

comment-period-timing.name: Comment period timing
comment-period-timing.plain: Short comment windows for complex rules, especially across holidays, limit how much the public and experts can take part.
comment-period-timing.check: Find comment, notice or hearing periods. Ask how long they run relative to the complexity of the proposal, whether they span holidays, and whether extensions are available.
comment-period-timing.fix: Set comment periods in proportion to complexity and allow extension on request.
comment-period-timing.ex_ai: Short comment windows for complex rules, including over holidays, limit public participation.
comment-period-timing.ex_other: For illustration: A land use rule of several hundred pages might open for comment for thirty days over a holiday period.

committee-forum-shopping.name: Committee assignment shapes the bill
committee-forum-shopping.plain: The committee a bill is sent to sets the expertise, priorities and interests that shape its text, so routing can influence the result.
committee-forum-shopping.check: Identify which committee or body drafted or reviewed the bill. Ask whether its jurisdiction fits the subject, which other bodies had a claim, and how that routing could have shaped the wording.
committee-forum-shopping.fix: Provide joint or sequential referral to bodies with relevant expertise.
committee-forum-shopping.ex_ai: Committee assignment sets the lens through which a bill is written, so routing to one committee over another shapes the result.
committee-forum-shopping.ex_other: For illustration: A bill on school food might go to a committee focused on agriculture, framing it around crop supply and not child nutrition.

compute-thresholds.name: Thresholds tied to an aging proxy
compute-thresholds.plain: A threshold set in a technical measure can stop tracking the real risk as technology changes, and can bind only the largest actors while leaving similar risks uncovered.
compute-thresholds.check: Find every numeric threshold. Ask what it is measured in, whether that measure will still track the risk in five years, and whether an actor can stay just under it.
compute-thresholds.fix: Pair thresholds with a risk based test and an update process, and add anti-evasion language.
compute-thresholds.ex_ai: Thresholds set to capture only the largest labs impose costs that only well-resourced firms can handle and leave others unregulated.
compute-thresholds.ex_other: For illustration: A chemical plant safety law might apply by storage volume of one substance, missing equally dangerous plants using a substitute.

conditional-cascades.name: Chained prerequisites
conditional-cascades.plain: Each provision may be reasonable alone, but when each waits on an earlier step, the whole depends on a long chain where one delay can stall everything.
conditional-cascades.check: Map provisions that begin only after another step finishes. Ask how long the full chain could take, who controls each step, and what happens if one is late.
conditional-cascades.fix: Set independent deadlines and default start dates that apply if a prior step is late.
conditional-cascades.ex_ai: Provisions that each require an earlier step can be reasonable alone but together make implementation depend on a long chain.
conditional-cascades.ex_other: For illustration: A broadband grant law might require a map, then a study, then a rule, then an application round, each starting only after the last.

consent-fiction.name: Consent by clicking agree
consent-fiction.plain: Treating acceptance of lengthy terms as consent meets the law's wording while giving people little real choice or understanding.
consent-fiction.check: Find where consent, opt-in or agreement is required. Ask what counts as consent, whether it can be bundled with the service, and whether a person can say no and still receive it.
consent-fiction.fix: Require specific, separate, revocable consent and bar making service depend on unneeded consent.
consent-fiction.ex_ai: Treating a click on lengthy terms as consent satisfies the law's wording while giving users little real choice.
consent-fiction.ex_other: For illustration: A health records law might accept a patient's signature on a long intake form as consent to sharing with unnamed partners.

content-neutrality-deflection.name: Neutral framing of amplification
content-neutrality-deflection.plain: Describing a process as neutral about content can place its effects outside rules written about content, even when the process determines what reaches people.
content-neutrality-deflection.check: Find claims that a process or function is neutral. Ask whether rules aimed at content or conduct would still reach it, and whether amplification or selection is covered as a separate activity.
content-neutrality-deflection.fix: Regulate the selection and amplification function directly, not only the underlying content.
content-neutrality-deflection.ex_ai: Treating algorithmic curation as content neutral leaves amplification of harmful material outside rules aimed at content.
content-neutrality-deflection.ex_other: For illustration: A broadcasting rule on misleading ads might not reach a service that merely orders ads by response rate.

contract-supremacy.name: Contract terms override public law
contract-supremacy.plain: Without a bar on waiver, standard form contracts can set aside protections the statute gives, so the protection depends on what a party signs.
contract-supremacy.check: Find any rights or duties stated as defaults. Ask whether a contract, waiver or agreement can alter them, and whether the text says protections cannot be waived.
contract-supremacy.fix: Add an anti-waiver clause and treat contrary terms as void.
contract-supremacy.ex_ai: Without anti-waiver provisions, contracts of adhesion can set aside protections the statute gives.
contract-supremacy.ex_other: For illustration: A tenant rights bill might not say lease terms cannot waive repair duties, so landlords can add a standard waiver.

counterfactual-framing.name: Counterfactual comparison
counterfactual-framing.plain: Comparing an effect with what would have happened anyway can make the added contribution of a practice look small and weaken the case for acting on it.
counterfactual-framing.check: Find tests that ask what would have happened without the practice. Ask who defines the alternative, whether it is realistic, and whether the test could erase an effect that is large in total.
counterfactual-framing.fix: Specify how the alternative is defined and also measure total effect.
counterfactual-framing.ex_ai: Comparing impact against what would have happened anyway makes the added contribution of a technology look small.
counterfactual-framing.ex_other: For illustration: A pollution permit rule might judge a new plant against likely emissions from other sources, so its addition looks minor.

damages-caps.name: Caps on damages and liability
damages-caps.plain: Statutory caps limit what injured people can recover, so losses above the cap fall on them and not on the party responsible.
damages-caps.check: Find limits on recovery, penalties or liability. Ask what the cap is, whether it is indexed, whether it applies per claim or in total, and what injuries could exceed it.
damages-caps.fix: Remove caps, or index them and set them at levels that cover realistic losses.
damages-caps.ex_ai: Statutory caps limit what injured people can recover, so losses above the cap fall on them instead of the company.
damages-caps.ex_other: For illustration: A transport safety law might cap total liability for a single accident at a figure far below the cost of a major incident.

damages-vs-injunction.name: Money only remedies
damages-vs-injunction.plain: If the only remedy is a fine, violations can be treated as a cost of doing business, while the power to stop a practice is a stronger deterrent.
damages-vs-injunction.check: Find the available remedies. Ask whether a court or agency can order a practice halted, a product withdrawn or conduct corrected, or whether money is the only consequence.
damages-vs-injunction.fix: Add injunctive relief and power to order a stop alongside monetary penalties.
damages-vs-injunction.ex_ai: Remedies limited to fines treat violations as a cost of business, while the ability to halt a system is a stronger deterrent.
damages-vs-injunction.ex_other: For illustration: A fisheries law might allow only fines for overfishing, with no power to suspend a vessel's license.

data-moat.name: Rules that entrench existing holders
data-moat.plain: Limits on gathering new resources can leave established firms with what they already hold while newcomers start with nothing, so a protective rule can also reduce competition.
data-moat.check: Find rules that restrict collecting or acquiring an input. Ask whether existing holders keep their stock, whether entrants face the full restriction, and how the effect on competition was weighed.
data-moat.fix: Apply restrictions to existing holdings in a comparable way or give entrants access to shared inputs.
data-moat.ex_ai: Privacy rules limiting new collection can leave established firms with historic data while new entrants have none.
data-moat.ex_other: For illustration: A licensing rule closing new permits for a resource might leave early permit holders with all of the supply.

data-portability.name: Weak portability standards
data-portability.plain: If moving data or accounts is hard or limited, switching costs remain high, so the law can appear to promote competition while changing little.
data-portability.check: Find portability or transfer rights. Ask what format, scope and timing are required, whether the receiving party can use the result, and whether the right is enforceable in practice.
data-portability.fix: Require standard formats, full scope, timely transfer and ongoing access for the receiving party.
data-portability.ex_ai: Weak portability standards preserve switching costs while appearing pro-competitive.
data-portability.ex_other: For illustration: A banking bill might let customers download statements as images, which cannot be loaded into another provider's system.

de-minimis-exception.ex_ai: A minimum size below which a deployment is ignored can exempt many small deployments that together have large effects.

deepfake-definition.name: Narrow definition of covered content
deepfake-definition.plain: A tight definition of the content or conduct regulated can exclude close variants that cause the same harm, so the rule covers less than people expect.
deepfake-definition.check: Find the definition of the prohibited content or conduct. Ask which realistic variants it leaves out, whether it requires a particular method or appearance, and how it handles new forms.
deepfake-definition.fix: Define by the harm caused and not the method used, with a process to update.
deepfake-definition.ex_ai: A narrow deepfake definition can exclude fake news text, synthetic images of invented events and made-up quotes.
deepfake-definition.ex_other: For illustration: A forgery law might define covered documents by physical paper form, leaving electronic copies outside it.

deployer-developer-split.name: Duties divided across supply stages
deployer-developer-split.plain: When duties are split between those who make a product and those who use it, each can point to the other unless the text says who is answerable for what.
deployer-developer-split.check: Find every actor named in the supply chain. Ask what each must do, who answers when the harm arises between stages, and whether a party can avoid duties by labeling itself as another stage.
deployer-developer-split.fix: Assign each duty to a named stage and add a default responsible party where roles overlap.
deployer-developer-split.ex_ai: When duties are divided between those who build and those who use a system without a clear rule, each can point to the other.
deployer-developer-split.ex_other: For illustration: A medical device law might require makers to test and hospitals to monitor, with no rule for failures that fall between.

displacement-vs-augmentation.name: Covers the stark form only
displacement-vs-augmentation.plain: A rule aimed at outright replacement can miss gradual change that reaches the same result in steps, so the covered event may never formally occur.
displacement-vs-augmentation.check: Find the event that triggers coverage. Ask whether a gradual path to the same result, in smaller steps, would avoid it, and whether the rule looks at cumulative effect.
displacement-vs-augmentation.fix: Cover cumulative and incremental change, not only a single defined event.
displacement-vs-augmentation.ex_ai: Regulating only replacement of workers leaves out augmentation that often turns into replacement over time.
displacement-vs-augmentation.ex_other: For illustration: A layoff notice law might apply to eliminated positions, not to hours cut each quarter until the job is gone.

dormant-commerce-weaponization.name: Exposure to structural legal challenge
dormant-commerce-weaponization.plain: A provision that may conflict with limits on the enacting body's power can attract litigation, and the result or the threat of it can support arguments for a weaker uniform standard.
dormant-commerce-weaponization.check: Find provisions that reach beyond the enacting body's territory or powers. Ask whether they are open to a structural legal challenge and what a loss would do to the rest of the law.
dormant-commerce-weaponization.fix: Tie reach to local effects, add findings and severability, and avoid needless extraterritorial reach.
dormant-commerce-weaponization.ex_ai: Vulnerable state laws can generate litigation that supports arguments for a weaker federal standard.
dormant-commerce-weaponization.ex_other: For illustration: A state labeling law might regulate out of state sales, drawing a challenge that ends in a weaker national standard.

due-process-hooks.name: Due process vulnerability
due-process-hooks.plain: Strong procedures paired with vague standards can invite due process challenges that remove enforcement while the law remains on the books.
due-process-hooks.check: Find enforcement powers and the standards they apply. Ask whether affected parties get fair notice, a hearing and a clear rule, or whether vagueness leaves the power open to challenge.
due-process-hooks.fix: Pair strong powers with clear standards, notice, hearing and appeal rights.
due-process-hooks.ex_ai: Aggressive procedures with vague standards invite due process challenges that can remove enforcement while leaving the law in place.
due-process-hooks.ex_other: For illustration: A licensing law might allow immediate suspension for conduct harmful to the public, with no defined test or hearing.

emotional-ai-gap.name: New product type outside existing categories
emotional-ai-gap.plain: A new kind of product may fit no existing category, so it can be argued that existing law already handles it or does not reach it.
emotional-ai-gap.check: Find the categories the law uses. Ask whether a new or hybrid product fits any of them, and whether silence could be read as covered by other law or as not covered.
emotional-ai-gap.fix: Name the new product type, or add a catch-all rule for products fitting no listed category.
emotional-ai-gap.ex_ai: AI companions may not fit existing categories, so it can be argued that existing law is enough or does not apply.
emotional-ai-gap.ex_other: For illustration: A toy safety law might cover physical toys and listed games, leaving a new connected toy that fits neither category.

evidentiary-trail.name: Record retention missing
evidentiary-trail.plain: Without a duty to keep records, a party can minimize what it logs, which makes later review and accountability difficult.
evidentiary-trail.check: Find duties to keep logs or records. Ask whether a retention period, content and format are set, who can access them, and whether a party could avoid creating the records at all.
evidentiary-trail.fix: Require creation and retention of defined records for a set period, with access for enforcers.
evidentiary-trail.ex_ai: Without record retention duties, systems can minimize logging, which makes later accountability difficult.
evidentiary-trail.ex_other: For illustration: A food safety rule might require tests but no storage of results, so past outbreaks cannot be traced.

export-control-definition.name: Narrow definition of controlled items
export-control-definition.plain: Defining controlled items narrowly can cover listed products while the methods, knowledge or close substitutes that give the same capability move freely.
export-control-definition.check: Find the definition of what is controlled. Ask whether it covers methods, know-how, components and substitutes, or only named items, and how the list is updated.
export-control-definition.fix: Define by capability, include know-how and components, and update the list on a schedule.
export-control-definition.ex_ai: Narrow definitions of controlled technology cover specific models while training methods and know-how move freely.
export-control-definition.ex_other: For illustration: A weapons control law might list finished devices while exempting the design files needed to build them.

fee-funded-dependency.name: Regulator funded by those it regulates
fee-funded-dependency.plain: An agency funded by fees from the parties it oversees may face budget pressure if it enforces strongly, which can shape its choices.
fee-funded-dependency.check: Find the source of the regulator's funding. Ask whether fee revenue depends on the number or goodwill of regulated parties, and whether the budget is protected from their influence.
fee-funded-dependency.fix: Fund through stable appropriations or fees set and collected independently of enforcement outcomes.
fee-funded-dependency.ex_ai: A regulator funded by fees from those it regulates may face budget pressure when it enforces strongly.
fee-funded-dependency.ex_other: For illustration: A securities body paid by firm registration fees might hesitate to take actions that drive firms to a competing registry.

first-amendment-engineering.name: Provisions exposed to speech challenge
first-amendment-engineering.plain: A slightly overbroad provision can be struck on speech grounds, and the ruling can narrow what later laws are able to do.
first-amendment-engineering.check: Find provisions that restrict or compel communication. Ask whether they are tailored to a stated interest, whether they are open to a speech challenge, and what a loss would mean for the rest of the law.
first-amendment-engineering.fix: Tailor narrowly, state the interest, add severability and avoid needless content based triggers.
first-amendment-engineering.ex_ai: Slightly overbroad provisions may be struck, and the resulting decision can narrow regulatory space for a generation.
first-amendment-engineering.ex_other: For illustration: A disclosure law might compel detailed statements from any publisher, inviting a challenge that sets a broad precedent.

foreseeable-harm.name: Foreseeability requirement
foreseeable-harm.plain: Limiting liability to harm that could be foreseen leaves out unexpected outcomes, which can be the main concern with complex products.
foreseeable-harm.check: Find liability or duty standards that depend on foreseeability. Ask who judges what was foreseeable, with what information, and whether unexpected but preventable harm would escape.
foreseeable-harm.fix: Base duties on risk assessment and monitoring, with responsibility for harms that testing would have revealed.
foreseeable-harm.ex_ai: Limiting liability to foreseeable harm leaves out unexpected behavior of complex systems, which is a main concern.
foreseeable-harm.ex_other: For illustration: A product law might impose liability only for foreseeable misuse, so a surprising failure mode leaves buyers without recourse.

future-benefits.name: Speculative benefits weighed against harm
future-benefits.plain: Cost-benefit rules that count uncertain future gains against documented present harms can tip decisions toward inaction.
future-benefits.check: Find cost-benefit or balancing tests. Ask whether benefits and harms are held to the same evidence standard, who estimates them, and whether projected gains can outweigh present harm.
future-benefits.fix: Require equal evidence standards and separate treatment of documented harm.
future-benefits.ex_ai: Cost-benefit rules that count uncertain future gains against documented present harms can tip decisions toward inaction.
future-benefits.ex_other: For illustration: A water quality rule might weigh projected industry growth against current contamination data.

geographic-demographic-aggregation.name: Aggregation hides concentrated harm
geographic-demographic-aggregation.plain: Measuring effects across a whole population can hide harms concentrated in particular places or groups, so a law may look like it works while some are hurt.
geographic-demographic-aggregation.check: Find how effects are measured. Ask whether results are broken out by place, group and sector, and whether a harm concentrated in a small area would be visible in the total.
geographic-demographic-aggregation.fix: Require breakdowns by place and group and set triggers for local effects.
geographic-demographic-aggregation.ex_ai: Measuring effects across the whole workforce or population can hide harms concentrated in particular places or groups.
geographic-demographic-aggregation.ex_other: For illustration: An air quality report might average readings statewide, hiding unsafe levels next to one industrial site.

harm-definition.name: Narrow definition of harm
harm-definition.plain: Requiring harm that is individual, direct and demonstrable can exclude diffuse or systemic harms that no single person can prove.
harm-definition.check: Find how harm is defined. Ask whether it requires direct or individual injury, whether collective, gradual or risk based harm counts, and who must prove it.
harm-definition.fix: Include diffuse, systemic and risk based harms and allow proof by statistical or group evidence.
harm-definition.ex_ai: Requiring individual, demonstrable, direct harm excludes diffuse or systemic harms that no single person can prove.
harm-definition.ex_other: For illustration: A privacy law might require a concrete financial loss, so exposure of many people's information is not actionable.

humans-in-the-loop.name: Nominal human review
humans-in-the-loop.plain: A requirement for human review can create the look of oversight when the reviewer lacks time, information or authority to depart from the recommended result.
humans-in-the-loop.check: Find required human review or sign-off. Ask whether the reviewer has the time, training, information and power to disagree, and whether outcomes show how often they do.
humans-in-the-loop.fix: Define meaningful review, give reviewers authority and time, and track override rates.
humans-in-the-loop.ex_ai: A human review requirement can create the appearance of oversight when reviewers tend to accept the system's output.
humans-in-the-loop.ex_other: For illustration: A loan rule might require an officer to sign each decision, though the officer has seconds per file and rarely overrules the score.

impact-without-teeth.name: Assessments without effect
impact-without-teeth.plain: Assessments that only inform, and do not affect whether or how something goes ahead, show people the harm while the project proceeds unchanged.
impact-without-teeth.check: Find required assessments or statements. Ask whether any finding can delay, change or stop the activity, who can act on it, and whether the public can respond.
impact-without-teeth.fix: Tie assessment findings to conditions, mitigation duties or review before the activity proceeds.
impact-without-teeth.ex_ai: Informational assessments that do not affect deployment decisions show communities their harm while deployment goes ahead.
impact-without-teeth.ex_other: For illustration: A development law might require a community impact report that expressly cannot hold up a building permit.

incident-definition.name: Incident reporting definitions
incident-definition.plain: Definitions that require serious or physical harm can leave out near misses, gradual harm and group effects, so the reports miss early warnings.
incident-definition.check: Find what counts as a reportable incident. Ask whether it requires material or physical harm, whether near misses and gradual or statistical harm count, and who decides.
incident-definition.fix: Include near misses and gradual harm and set objective reporting triggers.
incident-definition.ex_ai: Incident definitions requiring physical harm or materiality exclude near-misses, statistical discrimination and gradual harms.
incident-definition.ex_other: For illustration: A rail safety law might require reports only of accidents with injuries, missing repeated signal failures that caused none.

incumbent-compliance-costs.name: Compliance costs favor incumbents
incumbent-compliance-costs.plain: Heavy compliance requirements can act as barriers that large firms absorb and smaller or community competitors cannot, so a safeguard can also reduce competition.
incumbent-compliance-costs.check: Find registration, licensing and compliance program duties. Ask what they cost, whether small actors can meet them, and whether duties scale with size and risk.
incumbent-compliance-costs.fix: Scale duties to size and risk and provide support or simplified paths for small actors.
incumbent-compliance-costs.ex_ai: Heavy compliance requirements can act as barriers that large firms can absorb and smaller or open source competitors cannot.
incumbent-compliance-costs.ex_other: For illustration: A food safety bill might require a full time compliance officer, which a small producer cannot afford.

individualizing-systemic-harm.name: Individual proof for systemic harm
individualizing-systemic-harm.plain: Requiring one person to prove one cause for one injury cannot address effects that are visible only across many people.
individualizing-systemic-harm.check: Find the proof needed to bring or win a claim. Ask whether it demands individual causation, and whether group, statistical or pattern evidence is accepted.
individualizing-systemic-harm.fix: Accept pattern and statistical evidence and allow enforcers and groups to act on systemic harm.
individualizing-systemic-harm.ex_ai: Frameworks that require one person to prove one system caused one injury cannot address effects visible only across populations.
individualizing-systemic-harm.ex_other: For illustration: A pollution claim might require each resident to prove a specific illness came from one plant, though only area wide rates show the effect.

innovation-defense.name: Competitiveness findings
innovation-defense.plain: Findings that regulation could leave a country behind can be cited later in rulemaking and cost-benefit analysis, shifting how the operative rules are read.
innovation-defense.check: Find findings or purpose statements about competitiveness, growth or leadership. Ask whether they are tied to operative text and could be used to narrow duties or justify exemptions.
innovation-defense.fix: Keep findings balanced and state that they do not limit protective duties.
innovation-defense.ex_ai: Findings that regulation could cause the country to fall behind competitors can shape later rulemaking and cost-benefit analysis.
innovation-defense.ex_other: For illustration: A telecom bill might include a finding that regulation threatens leadership, later cited to justify weaker rules.

insurance-omission.name: No insurance requirement
insurance-omission.plain: Without required insurance or financial backing, no outside party assesses the risk and there may be no money available for injured people.
insurance-omission.check: Find whether risky activity must be backed by insurance, a bond or other security. Ask who pays if the responsible party cannot, and whether coverage amounts match realistic losses.
insurance-omission.fix: Require insurance or a bond sized to realistic losses.
insurance-omission.ex_ai: Without mandatory liability insurance, there is no outside assessment of risk and no guaranteed funds for injured people.
insurance-omission.ex_other: For illustration: A mining law might set cleanup duties but require no bond, leaving costs unpaid if the operator goes bankrupt.

international-harmonization.name: Duty to align with outside partners
international-harmonization.plain: A duty to consult or align with other jurisdictions before acting can delay action until consensus is reached, which can take years.
international-harmonization.check: Find duties to consult, coordinate or harmonize with other governments or bodies. Ask whether action must wait, what happens if no agreement emerges, and whether a deadline applies.
international-harmonization.fix: Allow consultation to proceed in parallel, with deadlines and authority to act alone.
international-harmonization.ex_ai: A duty to consult or align with international partners can delay action until consensus is reached, which may take years.
international-harmonization.ex_other: For illustration: A product safety bill might require agreement with trading partners on standards before any rule is issued.

interoperability.name: Interoperability mandates or absence
interoperability.plain: Without interoperability, network effects can lock in leading providers, so whether to require it is a decision about market structure.
interoperability.check: Find whether systems must work with others. Ask what standards, access and timing apply, and whether silence leaves leading providers able to keep users in.
interoperability.fix: Require open, documented standards and access for competing providers.
interoperability.ex_ai: Without interoperability, network effects lock in leading providers, so the choice is a market structure decision.
interoperability.ex_other: For illustration: A payments bill might say nothing about connecting to other networks, leaving users tied to the largest one.

ip-interactions.name: Intellectual property shields from inspection
ip-interactions.plain: Patents, copyright and trade secret protection can limit outside inspection and competition, which may block audits or reuse that the law otherwise expects.
ip-interactions.check: Find disclosure and inspection duties. Ask whether trade secret or other intellectual property claims can block access, and whether confidential review by auditors or regulators is guaranteed.
ip-interactions.fix: Provide confidential access for regulators and auditors that overrides trade secret objections.
ip-interactions.ex_ai: Patents, copyrightable outputs and trade secret model weights together can limit auditing and competition.
ip-interactions.ex_other: For illustration: A drug pricing law might require cost disclosure but let firms withhold figures as trade secrets.
